text:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: PagerDuty alert fired for service=redis-cache, symptom=ERR max number of clients reached, severity=critical, triggered_by=monitoring/redis-maxclients. Page sent to @eng-oncall (PD escalation policy: primary -> secondary).

pagerduty-bot: PagerDuty incident  INC-6321 opened, urgency=high. Please ack to stop repeat paging.

Alex K: acked (oncall) :raising_hand:

Alex K: seeing spikes in `connected_clients` to ~65k vs `maxclients` 65536? wait values look off — pulling `INFO clients` now.

Maria S: reported errors from frontend: `RedisError: ERR max number of clients reached` starting ~09:07 UTC, 09:10 ramping. Some API 503s for cache hits.

Lee: metrics: connection attempts backlog spiking, p50 latency for redis up to 200ms, p95 800ms. Traffic spike from a scheduled batch job in worker cluster `batch-worker-3` (owner: data-pipelines).

Alex K: quick mitigation plan: 1) throttle batch job, 2) kill noisy client sockets if we can identify them, 3) `CONFIG SET maxclients` bump temporarily, 4) enable degraded cache mode in API gateway for non-essential routes. Executing step 1 now: asking @data-pipelines to pause.

Maria S: data-pipelines confirmed pausing batch job (DM: @matt). Confirming pause took effect at 09:12 UTC.

Alex K: running `redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 INFO clients` -> code block:
```
# Clients
connected_clients:65534
client_longest_output_list:0
client_biggest_input_buf:0
blocked_clients:120
```

Alex K: also saw many clients from `10.12.48.*` (worker pool). I'm going to try targeted kill for clients with no throughput: `redis-cli CLIENT LIST | grep 10.12.48 | awk -F 'addr=' '{print $2}' | cut -d ' ' -f1 | xargs -n1 -I{} redis-cli CLIENT KILL {}` — doing it carefully.

Lee: +1 for CLIENT KILL on persistent storming IPs. Also recommend `CONFIG SET maxclients 100000` as immediate lift (we have headroom on kernel ulimits?), check ulimit first.

Alex K: checked ulimit on servers, no current soft cap that blocks up to 200k. Executing `CONFIG SET maxclients 100000` now.

Alex K: command returned OK. Monitoring connections.

Maria S: after bump, `connected_clients` dropped to ~18k over 2 minutes; blocked_clients down to 3. API 503s subsiding.

Nora: are we sure bumping maxclients is safe long-term? need follow-up: adjust client pools & fix runaway batch. I'll take ownership for the post-incident work.

Lee: agree. Temp bump is OK for now but we'll need: - client-side pooling defaults reduced - add circuit breaker on batch job - move non-critical cache to local LRU per worker - add alert to detect sudden client-count growth by source subnet.

Alex K: posting commands I ran:
```
# bump maxclients
redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 CONFIG SET maxclients 100000
# list candidates to kill
redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 CLIENT LIST | grep 10.12.48
# kill example client
redis-cli -h redis-prod-01 CLIENT KILL 10.12.48.13:50210
```

Maria S: verified application-level fallback: gateway routed 12% of calls to degraded cache path (no-ops) for non-critical endpoints. Reduced load by ~20%.

pagerduty-bot: Incident INC-6321 updated: status=acknowledged by Alex K.

Alex K: handing off to Nora for follow-up and RCA. Nora, will create a ticket for making the maxclients bump permanent only after safe changes? timeline 2 days for fixes.

Nora: acking handoff. I'll open CH-1452 (RCA + remediation). Immediate next steps: 1) coordinate with data-pipelines to ensure batch has exponential backoff 2) add ip-level surge detection to monitoring 3) implement graceful connection pooling defaults in our redis client wrapper.

Lee: note for RCA: we should also check for connection leaks in auth service — saw repeated reconnects in logs earlier.

Alex K: re-checking current numbers: p50 redis latency 28ms, p95 86ms, connected_clients 17,842. I think we can close the oncall page once PD notes updated.

pagerduty-bot: Notifying stakeholders: incident acknowledged, mitigation in place, monitoring recovery. Will auto-escalate in 10m if not resolved.

Maria S: customer impact: shortened cache failures for ~7% of requests for 6m window. No data loss. Customer-facing status: posted short blip to status page with note 'temporary cache errors, mitigation applied'.

Nora: creating follow-up ticket and assigning to data-pipelines + platform infra. ETA for permanent fix: 48-72 hours.

Alex K: thanks team. leaving a :white_check_mark: and removing myself from further escalation. Nora, ping me if you need help on the RCA.

Nora: will update when CH-1452 is created. closing thread once PD incident is resolved.

incident-bot: Incident INC-6321 marked as resolved by Alex K at 09:26 UTC (notes: temp maxclients bump + killed noisy clients + throttled batch job).
